summary.text: SETI, the search for extraterrestrial intelligence, is the set of efforts and scientific projects meant to detect extraterrestrial signals or other evidence of intelligent life beyond Earth.
Researchers monitor electromagnetic radiation, search for optical signals, and investigate possible extraterrestrial artifacts for signs of transmission from other civilizations.
Despite decades of searching, no confirmed evidence of alien intelligence has been found, which has drawn criticism of the field.

facts.label: Project Ozma
facts.value: Frank Drake's 1960 experiment, the first modern SETI experiment

facts.label: Wow! signal
facts.value: Strong signal noticed by volunteer Jerry Ehman on August 15, 1977

facts.label: Breakthrough Listen
facts.value: A $100 million, 10-year attempt to detect signals from nearby stars

facts.label: Big Ear
facts.value: Ohio State telescope behind the first continuous SETI program

facts.label: Suitcase SETI
facts.value: Portable spectrum analyzer with 131,000 narrow band channels

items.prompt: In 1959 two physicists argued for a particular region of the spectrum as the place to listen. Which region?

options.label: The microwave spectrum
The X-ray range
The visible light range
The ultraviolet range

items.explain: The 1959 paper first pointed out the possibility of searching the microwave spectrum, and proposed frequencies and initial targets.

items.prompt: A strong radio signal was caught once and scrawled with an exclamation. Why can't it count as confirmed evidence of aliens?

options.label: It came from an antenna with no clock
It was only ever recorded on paper
It was too weak to stand out at all
It never showed up again in later searches

items.explain: Some consider the Wow! signal the best candidate for an artificial extraterrestrial radio signal, but it has not been seen again, and no confirmed evidence has been found.

items.prompt: A lab wants a receiver that checks far more radio channels than the older banks of analog filters could. What technology does it use?

options.label: A bigger desktop spectrum analyzer
Digital signal processing with autocorrelation receivers
A second analog filter bank
A single-channel receiver, run for longer

items.explain: Analog filter banks limited the number of channels, but digital signal processing could build autocorrelation receivers to check far more.

items.prompt: A critic calls SETI speculative and unfalsifiable. How do its supporters see it?

options.label: As a proven way to reach other civilizations
As a crucial step in addressing the Fermi paradox
As a branch of conspiracy research
As a guaranteed route to confirmed discoveries

items.explain: Supporters see SETI as a crucial step in addressing the Fermi paradox and understanding extraterrestrial technosignatures.

items.prompt: A giant array of 1,500 dishes was designed in a NASA-funded study but never built. What became of the study?

options.label: It was forgotten and had no effect
It was built in secret in Ohio
It formed the basis of much of the SETI work that followed
It was replaced by an optical telescope

items.explain: Cyclops was not built, but its report formed the basis of much SETI work that followed.

items.prompt: SETI is often compared with UFO research and conspiracy theory. Why do supporters say that comparison is unfair?

options.label: It has already confirmed alien signals
It never uses any radio waves
It is run only by amateur hobbyists
It uses rigorous methods and verifiable data

items.explain: SETI remains a respected scientific field that relies on rigorous methods and verifiable data and research, despite the unwarranted skepticism.
